sources.reuse_limit: Custom Dataset Terms restrict redistribution and production or transfer of new maps. Original and every crop or other local derivative remain private.

correspondence.component_scope: eastern headward mountain feeder
correspondence.finding: The original whole-basin and geomorphological maps show the selected north–south then southwest mountain corridor in the northern/eastern basin, in the Salvias–Sinsao setting, continuing toward Portovelo. The selected headward stream is distinguished from the western Paccha/Huertas–Calera-side branches. Its geographic continuation is readable, while the initial feeder’s local name is not established.
correspondence.correspondence: observed at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: Small tributary names and exact source vertices are not required or assigned; mountain relief and generalized linework are used at corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Portovelo upper-valley junctions into the middle trunk
correspondence.finding: The mapped corridor runs southwest past the Sinsao/Portovelo valley into the converging upper network before the long westward trunk. The report independently identifies the Portovelo river as Amarillo and states that it joins Pindo downstream of the town. The selected route uses this Amarillo-side feeder, rather than assigning Pindo to all headwater branches.
correspondence.limits: The exact hydronym-change point and every small incoming branch are not established. Calera is a separate confluent tributary, not a name for this whole selected reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Balsas/Marcabelí to the westward Puyango corridor
correspondence.finding: The cartography follows the trunk west past the Santa Rufina–Balsas/Marcabelí setting, then along the northern side of the Ciano/El Limo country toward the international boundary. This matches the long westward section of FID13780. Report p.27 links Puyango usage to the Yaguachi junction near Balsas and describes the subsequent westward route.
correspondence.limits: Puyango applies to the observed middle-trunk context; no whole-FID scalar name is asserted because FID13780 also includes the separately described upper feeder and junction reaches.

correspondence.component_scope: northeastern border-corridor fragment
correspondence.finding: The original maps show the westward trunk meeting the international border and continuing southwest along its valley. The short selected border-aligned fragment occupies that same channel corridor, between the interior Ecuadorian middle reach and the next bend.
correspondence.limits: Selected border alignment is retained metadata, not proof of exact surveyed border/channel coincidence. No exact bank or every-bend agreement is required.

correspondence.component_scope: short intervening bend in the border river corridor
correspondence.finding: The short non-border-aligned selected bend lies within the same mapped southwestward Puyango border-valley continuation. The source cartography shows the intervening river corridor, with no lake, reservoir or missing overland connector needed between FIDs13781 and13783.
correspondence.limits: Its small triangular/generalized shape is not treated as a separately named tributary or independently revalidated geometry.

correspondence.component_scope: southwestern border-corridor fragment
correspondence.finding: The river and border corridor continue southwest through the mapped hill country toward the major lower bend. The source covers the full short FID13783 continuation to the start of FID13784; this is not inferred solely from model connectivity.
correspondence.limits: No exact contemporary bank, boundary or vertex claim is made.

correspondence.component_scope: Cazaderos junction and westward-to-northward Tumbes bend
correspondence.finding: The acquired basin maps show the trunk continuing west along the southern bend, receiving the southern tributary corridor and then turning northwest/north through the confined valley toward Rica Playa. Report pp.27–28 identifies the Cazaderos confluence and the change to Tumbes, with Cabo Inga and downstream gauging context. These sources jointly establish the material upper/lower-system transition.
correspondence.limits: No exact coordinate for the name transition is asserted. The selected initial portion of this FID is not all relabeled Tumbes.

correspondence.component_scope: northward lower valley through Rica Playa and the Tumbes plain
correspondence.finding: The maps show the north-turning lower river past Rica Playa/Capitana, Higuerón, the Pampas de Hospital–San Jacinto valley and the city of Tumbes. Geomorphological valley and terrace units corroborate the selected lower corridor. Figure3 independently depicts the lower river through these same settlements before its delta bifurcation/avulsion zone.
correspondence.limits: Multiple dated channel positions are evidence of one river corridor, not exact modern bank agreement.

correspondence.component_scope: actual selected terminal: western historical delta/outlet corridor to the Pacific
correspondence.finding: At1:100,000, Figure3 shows older1961/1976/1986 Tumbes channels running northwest from the city and then north through the western delta toward the Pacific coast, matching the selected western terminal corridor. The2000 course shifts eastward toward a separate outlet. Report p.41 describes the1997/98 channel change into Estero Tamarindo and changing delta/coastal sedimentation. The selected actual sea terminus is therefore read as part of the historical Tumbes river outlet system rather than assumed to be today’s main mouth.
correspondence.limits: Present activity, present water allocation, a unique estero name for the selected western branch, exact tidal limits and source/render endpoint vertices are unverified. The diagram’s inset partially obscures the far western coastal corner, but dated channels, surrounding coastline and the whole-basin map together show the ordinary terminal corridor; no precise mouth-point match is required.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected headward Prata drainage, southeastern Felisburgo
correspondence.finding: Felisburgo original shows the stream corridor beside Cabeceira da Prata/Comunidade da Prata toward Vargem da Lapa, its connection with the Repouso drainage and then the eastward channel below the do Meio junction. The overlapping Rio do Prado map labels the southwestern feeder Córrego Prata and the connected eastward reach Córrego do Prado. Generalized geographic correspondence is established; the exact first modeled vertex is not declared an officially named spring.
correspondence.name_scope_limit: Prata is a local feeder label, not a uniform name assigned to the complete selected river. The precise initial short reach retains a null individual name.

correspondence.component_scope: Vila Formosa and the do Prado corridor to Palmópolis
correspondence.finding: Rio do Prado original follows the channel past Boa Sorte and Vila Formosa, through the Córrego Grande setting to Palmópolis. It labels the upstream part Córrego do Prado and the eastward river Rio do Prado ou Jucuruçu. Tributaries such as Prado Pequeno and Santa Isabel and the Bananeiras drainage at Palmópolis are distinct lateral waters. The Palmópolis map overlaps the same west-entry corridor.
correspondence.name_scope_limit: Bounded component observation only; no accepted whole-feature scalar name.

correspondence.component_scope: Palmópolis eastward bend, Jeribá and Bahia transition
correspondence.finding: Palmópolis original traces the connected river from the city eastward, down the large southward bend and toward the Jeribá settlement corridor, continuing into the Jucuruçu municipal setting. The river line and relevant tributary joins were visually followed; the green district boundary is a separate cartographic line and is not mistaken for the selected channel. INEMA2014 overlaps the Bahia continuation west of Jucuruçu town.
correspondence.name_scope_limit: Geographic passage is supported even where the municipal source has no printed reach label; no individual name invented.

correspondence.component_scope: Jucuruçu town and the eastbound northern arm
correspondence.finding: INEMA original shows the selected channel along the Jucuruçu town corridor with Jucuruçu and do Prado labels, below the northern Gado Bravo tributary system and past the Abril/São Domingos tributary setting. The mapped trunk then turns southeast and is explicitly labelled Rio Jucuruçu Braço Norte. The southern-arm drainage is geographically separate.
correspondence.name_scope_limit: Bounded component observation only; no accepted whole-feature scalar name.

correspondence.component_scope: Itamaraju and the lower northern arm
correspondence.finding: INEMA follows the northern arm through Itamaraju, the Rio do Ouro tributary junction and the BR101/BR489 road setting. It continues southeast past the Boa União tributary setting toward the southern-arm confluence. The original channel course, rather than town or basin proximity alone, supplies correspondence.
correspondence.name_scope_limit: Bounded component observation only; no accepted whole-feature scalar name.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern-arm confluence and combined lower Jucuruçu
correspondence.finding: INEMA original maps the separate Jucuruçu/Jacuruçu Braço Sul joining the northern arm northwest of Prado. The selected continuation proceeds from that junction toward the broad lower meanders. Colino I, Colino II and Cachoeira da Lixa hydroelectric symbols occur on the southern-arm tributary system, not on this selected northern-arm mainstem. No large lake or reservoir traversal is shown on the selected route at the inspected map scales. UFV prose independently describes the two-arm formation.
correspondence.name_scope_limit: Bounded component observation only; no accepted whole-feature scalar name.

correspondence.component_scope: Prado lower meanders and actual Atlantic outlet
correspondence.finding: INEMA original follows the combined river through its broad meandering lower waterway, below the Cotia and Leandro tributary settings, past the south side of Prado and through the coastal channel to the Atlantic shoreline. The river/coast connection and the adjacent coastal form were actually read. The Santo Antônio and Alcobaça/Itanhém outlets to the south are separate systems. Generalized mouth correspondence is sufficient; no exact bank or mouth-point alignment is asserted.
correspondence.name_scope_limit: Representative coastal-system identity only; no scalar river hydronym assigned to every estuarine water surface or tidal connector.

correspondence.component_scope: Somuncurá headward setting
correspondence.finding: The selected western head is on the Somuncurá basalt upland between the Cerro Loco and Cerro Mirasol sector, east of Cerro Corona. The original map shows small intermittent upland drainage and the southeastward descent past Cerro Bouzo toward La Polvareda. A separate Laguna Blanca lies northwest; the selected head is not assigned that lake as its source. The headward hydronym is unestablished.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Arroyo de la Ventana upper valley
correspondence.finding: From La Polvareda the corridor turns south by Campana Mahuida and the Sierra Nevada flank, then east past El Sauce, Salitral Grande and Carrizo toward Arroyo de la Ventana locality. The original channel carries the Ventana label. The line marked Acueducto is separately mapped infrastructure and is not treated as the stream.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Ventana–Los Berros material junction
correspondence.finding: East of the Arroyo de la Ventana locality the selected channel turns northeast through the lowland west of Mesada Blanca. The independently drawn Los Berros drainage descends from the northwest through Los Álamos and the El Sacrificio sector to this same trunk. The onward combined corridor turns east/northeast through the Los Tamariscos sector. The plan explicitly identifies the confluence of Ventana and Los Berros as forming Arroyo Salado. Exact channel/name-transition vertices are not assigned.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.mapped_reach_name: Ventana–Los Berros junction; downstream Salado system

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Salado lowland and highway crossing
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor continues northeast, then turns east by Las Violetas into the channel directly labeled Arroyo Salado. It follows the low-lying, intermittently drawn drainage through the La Aguadita sector, crosses the north–south RN 3 corridor north of Sierra Grande, then bends southeast through Los Tres Morros. Mapped small depressions and wet ground are part of the corridor setting, not separately renamed rivers or proof of continuous present flow.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Salado and separate tributaries
correspondence.finding: Downstream of Los Tres Morros, the selected channel passes El Salado estancia and turns southeast along the western side of Loma Moncho. A separately mapped tributary arrives from the El Porvenir / Sierra Grande area to the west. The Salado corridor then passes El Pedregal and the San Miguel sector toward the small coastal lagoon/estuarine expansion. A separate farther-south drainage through the San Francisco sector is not substituted for the selected mainstem.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The lower Salado corridor opens into a small coastal water body north of the historical Balneario El Salado label, then a narrow outlet reaches the western Golfo San Matías coast beside that locality. Original mapping shows both the final inlet/outlet setting and the sea. The coastal chapter independently identifies the Arroyo Salado mouth and equates Balneario El Salado with Playas Doradas. No precise bank, mouth vertex or current opening condition is asserted.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Headward opening and long southward approach
correspondence.finding: The opening and long southward sequence lie on the mapped continental Inland Ice, inland and west of the coastal nunatak belt. The original shows continuous ice geography throughout this approach, with ice surface contours and thickness shading. No natural-river source, named channel or tributary identity is established.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.
correspondence.limits: The positive observation is the ice setting, not river continuity, subglacial flow or a claim that each modeled step is a natural channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward-to-eastward turn and first eastward connector
correspondence.finding: The turn and first long eastward sequence remain in the mapped Inland Ice west of the Bildsøe Nunatakker belt. The entire connector is visible on the retained original, including the small northward bend before the route continues east-southeast. No lake passage or named receiving river is established.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.
correspondence.limits: Blue ice-contour lines and black sub-ice bedrock contours are not adopted as channels.

correspondence.component_scope: Bildsøe Nunatakker ice/rock transition
correspondence.finding: The east-southeast sequence passes through the southern part of the mapped nunatak-belt setting. The source separates exposed rock bodies from intervening ice and shows the surrounding connector into the ice corridor farther east. Bildsøe Nunatakker is a terrain-group label on the national original, not a representative river identity.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.
correspondence.limits: This national-scale reading does not assign every short modeled step to a precise rock boundary or ice bank. No unresolved major geographic gap remains.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern ice corridor and approach to the narrow coastal strip
correspondence.finding: The remaining eastward sequence traverses the mapped ice corridor between the nunatak belt and the narrow exposed-rock coastal strip along the western side of the Jøkelbugten region. The later northward bend and following eastward/southward progression occupy that ice-to-coastal-land setting. The source provides both sides and the connecting setting; no unseen lake, reservoir or river confluence is inferred.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.
correspondence.limits: The nearby Storstrømmen label belongs to the larger glacier corridor extending south. Neither it nor Jøkelbugten is transferred to the whole modeled feature.

correspondence.component_scope: Final coastal-land interval and actual ending
correspondence.finding: The actual ending is on the eastern coastal margin of the narrow bedrock strip in the southern Jøkelbugten setting, north of the separately labeled Skærfjorden. The national original distinguishes this coastal ending from the inland ice corridor and from the broader glacier corridor to the west/south. The selected terminal is geographically accounted for without assigning a nearby fjord or glacier name as a river name.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized terminal/corridor scale.
correspondence.limits: No fine-scale terminal inlet name is assigned. The retained model terminal class sea is metadata, not evidence of a surveyed natural river mouth, contemporary coastline or current ice-front position.
